question: Under a systems approach to medical error, near-miss events that did not cause patient harm need not be formally reported because they resulted in no adverse outcome.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. Near-miss events are among the most valuable safety data available because they expose system weaknesses without the ethical and legal complexity of a harm-causing event. Reporting them is a professional obligation under risk management frameworks, even when no patient was ultimately harmed.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. Near-miss reporting is a cornerstone of systems-based risk management. Near-misses reveal latent system vulnerabilities before they produce harm; suppressing them allows those vulnerabilities to persist. The NMC Competency Framework and patient safety standards emphasise that near-misses must be reported and reviewed.
